cards.name: Animate Land
cards.oracle_text: Until end of turn, target land becomes a 3/3 creature that's still a land.
cards.flavor_text: Irony is getting walked on by the earth instead of the other way around.

research.note: A cheap way to animate a Forest or Swamp without needing a botanical creature type.
research.caution: Does not untap the land or give haste; a newly played land may be unable to attack. The land is exposed to creature removal for the turn.
research.manaNote: Costs G; temporary animation.

cards.name: Awakener Druid
cards.oracle_text: When this creature enters, target Forest becomes a 4/5 green Treefolk creature for as long as this creature remains on the battlefield. It's still a land.
cards.flavor_text: The druids of Mazar treat each seedcone with respect for the warrior it will become.

research.note: Turns an actual Forest into a sizeable Treefolk, making the Druid a direct botanical support candidate.
research.caution: Animation lasts only while this Druid stays on the battlefield. It does not untap the Forest or give haste.
research.manaNote: Costs 2G and requires a Forest target.

cards.name: Embodiment of Insight
cards.oracle_text:
Vigilance
Land creatures you control have vigilance.
Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, you may have target land you control become a 3/3 Elemental creature with haste until end of turn. It's still a land.

research.note: Turns landfall into temporary animated lands and gives your land creatures vigilance, supporting Forests or Swamps equally.
research.caution: Five mana; animation is temporary. Landfall needs another land entering and the land is still vulnerable to creature removal.
research.manaNote: Costs 4G; works on any land you control.

cards.name: Hissing Quagmire
cards.oracle_text:
This land enters tapped.
{T}: Add {B} or {G}.
{1}{B}{G}: Until end of turn, this land becomes a 2/2 black and green Elemental creature with deathtouch. It's still a land.

research.note: A living mire that turns into a deathtouch Elemental; a strong swamp-themed lead and black/green mana source.
research.caution: Its actual land type is simply Land, not Swamp or Forest. Enters tapped; animation and attacking compete with its mana ability.
research.manaNote: Produces B or G; animating it costs 1BG.

cards.name: Kormus Bell
cards.oracle_text: All Swamps are 1/1 black creatures that are still lands.

research.note: The direct animated-Swamp lead: makes every Swamp a black creature without assigning a creature subtype.
research.caution: Affects opponents' Swamps too. Creature removal can now destroy lands, and new Swamps are subject to summoning sickness. A potentially disruptive research candidate.
research.manaNote: Costs 4 generic mana; needs actual Swamps or an effect that grants the Swamp subtype.

rulings.comment: A noncreature permanent that turns into a creature can attack, and its {T} abilities can be activated, only if its controller has continuously controlled that permanent since the beginning of their most recent turn. It doesn't matter how long the permanent has been a creature.
The lands are both lands and creatures at the same time. They are affected by anything that affects either permanent type.
It affects Swamps controlled by any and all players.

cards.name: Lair of the Hydra
cards.oracle_text:
If you control two or more other lands, this land enters tapped.
{T}: Add {G}.
{X}{G}: Until end of turn, this land becomes an X/X green Hydra creature. It's still a land. X can't be 0.

research.note: A green living-land candidate whose creature form is a Hydra; investigate the landscape connection regardless of creature type.
research.caution: Not actually a Forest. Enters tapped if you already control two other lands; activation needs extra mana beyond X.
research.manaNote: Produces G; animation costs XG with X greater than zero.

cards.name: Life and Limb
cards.oracle_text: All Forests and all Saprolings are 1/1 green Saproling creatures and Forest lands in addition to their other types. (They're affected by summoning sickness.)
cards.flavor_text:
"It was a sight of pain and awe—a twisted forest, migrating across the salt plain in search of richer soil."
—Edahlis, greenseeker

research.note: Directly joins Forests and Saprolings: all become both land and creature, linking living lands with the Fungi theme.
research.caution: Affects all players. New Forests cannot immediately tap for mana. With Sporemound, a land creates a Saproling land that triggers another token repeatedly; this mandatory loop needs careful review or exclusion.
research.manaNote: Costs 3G; a major rules-complexity and board-risk candidate rather than a routine inclusion.

rulings.comment: Each Forest and Saproling will have the card types creature and land, and the subtypes Forest and Saproling. Each subtype maintains its correlation to the proper type: Forest isn't a creature type and Saproling isn't a land type.
Each Forest has the ability "{T}: Add {G}."

Forests enter the battlefield as land creatures, and abilities that trigger whenever a creature enters the battlefield will trigger. Because you haven't controlled these creatures since your turn began, you can't pay the {T} cost of their mana ability.
Saprolings enter the battlefield as land creatures, and abilities that trigger whenever a land enters the battlefield will trigger.

cards.name: Living Lands
cards.oracle_text: All Forests are 1/1 creatures that are still lands.

research.note: Animates all actual Forests, regardless of whether their creature form has any botanical subtype.
research.caution: Applies to every player and exposes Forest mana bases to creature removal. Does not grant haste, so newly played Forests cannot immediately tap for mana.
research.manaNote: Costs 3G; actual Forest subtype matters.

cards.name: Llanowar Loamspeaker
cards.oracle_text:
{T}: Add one mana of any color.
{T}: Target land you control becomes a 3/3 Elemental creature with haste until end of turn. It's still a land. Activate only as a sorcery.
cards.flavor_text: Twigs broken underfoot in Llanowar tend to return the favor.

research.note: An Elf Druid included for what it does: fixes mana or turns a Forest, Swamp, or other land into a temporary Elemental.
research.caution: Its two tap abilities compete; land animation is sorcery-speed and does not untap the target land. Lower thematic priority because it is an Elf; compare non-Elf enablers first.
research.manaNote: Costs 1G and can produce any one color.

cards.name: Lumbering Falls
cards.oracle_text:
This land enters tapped.
{T}: Add {G} or {U}.
{2}{G}{U}: Until end of turn, this land becomes a 3/3 green and blue Elemental creature with hexproof. It's still a land.

research.note: A wooded waterfall becoming an Elemental fits the living-land research beyond literal Plant or Treefolk types.
research.caution: It is not actually a Forest. Enters tapped and requires both green and blue for animation.
research.manaNote: Produces G or U; animation costs 2GU.

cards.name: Natural Affinity
cards.oracle_text: All lands become 2/2 creatures until end of turn. They're still lands.
cards.flavor_text: As long as the dryads are a part of the forest, the forest is a part of the army.

research.note: A broad forest-or-swamp animation spell that turns all lands into creatures for a turn.
research.caution: Also gives the opponent an army and makes every land vulnerable to creature removal. Does not untap lands or give haste.
research.manaNote: Costs 2G at instant speed; high board complexity.

cards.name: Restless Cottage
cards.oracle_text:
This land enters tapped.
{T}: Add {B} or {G}.
{2}{B}{G}: This land becomes a 4/4 black and green Horror creature until end of turn. It's still a land.
Whenever this land attacks, create a Food token and exile up to one target card from a graveyard.

research.note: A haunted woodland land that becomes a Horror, with graveyard interaction and Food as additional thematic hooks.
research.caution: It is not actually a Forest or Swamp. Enters tapped; graveyard exile can interfere with either faction's recursion.
research.manaNote: Produces B or G; animation costs 2BG.

cards.name: Rude Awakening
cards.oracle_text:
Choose one —
• Untap all lands you control.
• Until end of turn, lands you control become 2/2 creatures that are still lands.
Entwine {2}{G} (Choose both if you pay the entwine cost.)
cards.set_name: Duel Decks Anthology: Garruk vs. Liliana

research.note: Can untap your lands, animate them, or do both: a possible living-forest or living-swamp finisher.
research.caution: Five mana for one mode, eight for both. Does not grant haste; newly played lands may be unable to attack.
research.manaNote: Costs 4G, plus entwine 2G for both modes.

cards.name: Sylvan Advocate
cards.oracle_text:
Vigilance
As long as you control six or more lands, this creature and land creatures you control get +2/+2.
cards.flavor_text: "The land gives of itself. Its abundance provides, even in times of chaos."

research.note: Supports animated lands directly with a late-game power boost, despite being an Elf Druid Ally.
research.caution: Its bonus needs six lands and strengthens land creatures, not every botanical creature or token. Lower thematic priority because it is an Elf; compare non-Elf enablers first.
research.manaNote: Costs 1G; no off-color requirement.

cards.name: Sylvan Awakening
cards.oracle_text: Until your next turn, all lands you control become 2/2 Elemental creatures with reach, indestructible, and haste. They're still lands.
cards.flavor_text:
"Yavimaya is aware, but not always awake. You will know the difference when you see it."
—Karn

research.note: Temporarily turns your Forests, Swamps, and other lands into protected Elementals with haste and reach.
research.caution: Does not untap the lands, so mana spending reduces immediate attackers. Indestructible does not protect against exile or all toughness reduction.
research.manaNote: Costs 2G; effect lasts until your next turn.

cards.name: Treetop Village
cards.oracle_text:
This land enters tapped.
{T}: Add {G}.
{1}{G}: This land becomes a 3/3 green Ape creature with trample until end of turn. It's still a land. (It can deal excess combat damage to the player or planeswalker it's attacking.)

research.note: A forest landscape animating as an Ape illustrates why living lands merit investigation regardless of creature subtype.
research.caution: Not actually a Forest. Enters tapped and its animation uses mana that cannot also cast a spell.
research.manaNote: Produces G; animation costs 1G.

cards.name: Nissa, Who Shakes the World
cards.oracle_text:
Whenever you tap a Forest for mana, add an additional {G}.
+1: Put three +1/+1 counters on up to one target noncreature land you control. Untap it. It becomes a 0/0 Elemental creature with vigilance and haste that's still a land.
−8: You get an emblem with "Lands you control have indestructible." Search your library for any number of Forest cards, put them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

all_parts.name: Nissa, Who Shakes the World Emblem

research.note: A Forest-focused planeswalker that can animate any of your noncreature lands into a vigilant Elemental and substantially increase green mana.
research.caution: A strong repeatable engine with planeswalker rules and a large mana advantage; animated lands remain exposed to creature removal. Its mana bonus specifically requires Forests.
research.manaNote: Costs 3GG; likely too strong for some introductory environments.

cards.name: Wrenn and Realmbreaker
cards.oracle_text:
Lands you control have "{T}: Add one mana of any color."
+1: Up to one target land you control becomes a 3/3 Elemental creature with vigilance, hexproof, and haste until your next turn. It's still a land.
−2: Mill three cards. You may put a permanent card from among the milled cards into your hand.
−7: You get an emblem with "You may play lands and cast permanent spells from your graveyard."

research.note: A Treefolk-associated planeswalker that animates any land as an Elemental and lets all your lands provide any color, tying land creatures to multicolor support.
research.caution: Adds planeswalker rules, milling, and graveyard play. Its animation is temporary and does not untap the land. The emblem allows normal play/casting rather than free spells.
research.manaNote: Costs 1GG before it can help fix other colors.

cards.name: Dryad Arbor
cards.oracle_text: (This land isn't a spell, it's affected by summoning sickness, and it has "{T}: Add {G}.")

research.note: A genuine Dryad that is also a Forest land, bridging woodland flavor with land and creature interactions.
research.caution: It is a Dryad, not a Plant. It is played as a land rather than cast as a spell, uses a land play, and cannot tap for mana immediately if affected by summoning sickness. Creature removal can also remove this mana source.
research.manaNote: Has no mana cost; its Forest subtype provides a green-mana tap ability.

cards.name: Woodcaller Automaton
cards.oracle_text:
Prototype {2}{G}{G} — 3/3 (You may cast this spell with different mana cost, color, and size. It keeps its abilities and types.)
When this creature enters, if you cast it, untap target land you control. It becomes a Treefolk creature with haste and base power and toughness equal to this creature's power and toughness. It's still a land.

research.note: A wood-themed Construct that explicitly turns one of your lands into a Treefolk creature, connecting a non-Treefolk card to genuine Treefolk support.
research.caution: The Automaton is a Construct, not a Treefolk. The land-animation trigger requires that the Automaton was cast, so merely returning it from a graveyard does not trigger it. Animating a land exposes mana to creature removal.
research.manaNote: Costs 10 normally or 2GG as a prototype; the animated land's base size uses the Automaton's power and toughness.

cards.name: Ambush Commander
cards.oracle_text:
Forests you control are 1/1 green Elf creatures that are still lands.
{1}{G}, Sacrifice an Elf: Target creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn.
cards.set_name: Duel Decks Anthology: Elves vs. Goblins

research.note: Animates your actual Forests, but makes them Elves and is an Elf itself. Keep this as a comparison candidate while preferring other ways to build a living-forest theme.
research.caution: Lower-priority thematic fit: the owner prefers to avoid turning the green packets into Elf decks. Its sacrifice ability can consume animated Forest lands; creature removal also threatens the mana base.
research.manaNote: Costs 3GG; its activated ability needs 1G and an Elf sacrifice.

cards.name: Awakening of Vitu-Ghazi
cards.oracle_text: Put nine +1/+1 counters on target land you control. It becomes a legendary 0/0 Elemental creature with haste named Vitu-Ghazi. It's still a land.
cards.flavor_text: The Eternal armies advanced on Vitu-Ghazi. At Nissa's command, Vitu-Ghazi advanced on them.

research.note: Animates a Forest, Swamp, or any other land into a huge legendary Elemental, using counters instead of depending on botanical creature types.
research.caution: A five-mana instant makes one very large threat and leaves a land exposed to creature removal. It does not untap the target land; the nine counters remain a significant power jump.
research.manaNote: Costs 3GG; grants haste but does not supply an untapped land.

cards.name: Brave the Wilds
cards.oracle_text:
Bargain (You may sacrifice an artifact, enchantment, or token as you cast this spell.)
If this spell was bargained, target land you control becomes a 3/3 Elemental creature with haste that's still a land.
Search your library for a basic land card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle.

research.note: Finds a basic land for color support and, when bargained, permanently animates an existing land as an Elemental. Spare Plants or Saprolings can pay the bargain cost.
research.caution: The basic land goes to hand, not the battlefield. Bargain requires sacrificing an artifact, enchantment, or token; the animated land is an existing target and becomes vulnerable to creature removal.
research.manaNote: Costs G; can find any basic land but needs an additional resource to animate a land.

cards.name: Fendeep Summoner
cards.oracle_text: {T}: Up to two target Swamps each become 3/5 Treefolk Warrior creatures in addition to their other types until end of turn.
cards.flavor_text: "What is drowned is not forgotten. I will fulfill my oath. Come back to me, my brethren, as I have come back for you."

research.note: A black Treefolk Shaman that turns up to two actual Swamps into sizeable Treefolk Warriors. A direct link between the Treefolk theme and a living-swamp plan without Elf support.
research.caution: Five mana and a tap ability mean it normally waits a turn before use. Animation does not untap the Swamps or grant haste; the targets can be any Swamps, including an opponent's.
research.manaNote: Costs 4B; activation costs tapping this creature and needs Swamp targets.

cards.name: Genju of the Cedars
cards.oracle_text:
Enchant Forest
{2}: Enchanted Forest becomes a 4/4 green Spirit creature until end of turn. It's still a land.
When enchanted Forest is put into a graveyard, you may return this card from your graveyard to your hand.
cards.set_name: Duel Decks Anthology: Garruk vs. Liliana

research.note: A Forest-bound Spirit enchantment: turns an actual Forest into a 4/4 green Spirit for a turn, then can recover the Aura if the Forest dies.
research.caution: Only enchants a Forest. Animation does not untap it or grant haste. The Aura can return from your graveyard when the Forest is put into a graveyard; the land itself is not recovered.
research.manaNote: Costs G, then 2 generic mana per animation.

cards.name: Genju of the Fens
cards.oracle_text:
Enchant Swamp
{2}: Until end of turn, enchanted Swamp becomes a 2/2 black Spirit creature with "{B}: This creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn." It's still a land.
When enchanted Swamp is put into a graveyard, you may return this card from your graveyard to your hand.
cards.set_name: Duel Decks Anthology: Garruk vs. Liliana

research.note: The swamp counterpart to Genju of the Cedars: animates an actual Swamp as a black Spirit with a repeatable temporary power-and-toughness boost.
